extraction.body: The City of Memphis has issued an enhanced security plan for forthcoming Memphis City Council meetings following protests that ultimately shut down the council's Oct. 9 meeting. Memphis City Council Chief Administrative Officer Takeyshia Johnson on Monday, Oct. 19, circulated a memo to council members and staff titled "ACTION REQUIRED: October 20 Council Meetings| Enhanced Security Procedures" that outlines additional security measures to be taken at the City Council's Tuesday, Oct. 20, and Nov. 10 meetings, as well as committee meetings scheduled to take place in the coming weeks. The memo was filed alongside other court documents related to a temporary restraining order filed by Rep. Justin J. Pearson, who was suspended by the City of Memphis from attending the next two council meetings for his alleged role in the Oct. 9 upheaval. Several other people who attended the Oct. 9 meeting, including at least one council member, have also been suspended from the next two meetings. The security plan outlines additional steps to be taken, including increased security personnel, reserved seating, strict capacity restrictions, and a clear-bag policy. "This work is informed not only by what occurred on October 6, but also by our staff's experiences and concerns," Johnson's email reads. "Since that meeting, staff members have received threats, endured concerning phone calls, and expressed serious concerns about their physical safety and emotional well-being." In addition to the clear-bag policy and reserved seating, under the enhanced security plan, public access to the dais will be restricted, the public speaking podium will be relocated behind the chamber gates, front-row seating will be reserved for "speakers, honorees, presenters and the media," and anyone who is removed for disruptive behavior will not be able to return until at least the following meeting. The plan also halts all unannounced visits to the City Council offices: "Until further notice, access to the Council office will be limited to individuals with confirmed appointments. Walk-ins and unannounced visits will not be permitted." The measures are expected to be in place by Tuesday's council meeting, with some provisions, including restrictions on council chamber access, to remain in effect beyond the two meetings specifically mentioned. extraction.body: The transportation tax measure was intended to fill the gap left by Measure C. Councilmember Miguel Arias called for the special meeting ahead of a 5 p.m. deadline Wednesday. Residents waited about two hours for the meeting to begin before learning no action would be taken. "You called a meeting, we showed up," attendees chanted during the meeting. Another resident said, "They are failing to represent us." Ariana Martinez Lott, a Fresno resident, criticized elected officials for not attending. "What we often see is that when elected officials, when they're campaigning, they're always showing up and they're asking us to support them. Then when they're asked to do their jobs, they play political games this way," Martinez Lott said. Council members Miguel Arias, Brandon Vang and Nick Richardson were present and waiting for another member to arrive. As the deadline approached, it became clear a quorum would not be reached. "We will not be holding a special Fresno City Council meeting today," Vice President Vang announced. Following the meeting, Arias spoke with Action News after the decision. "Our intention was never to have two local taxes for residents in the city of Fresno," Arias said. Wednesday's special meeting follows action taken Tuesday by the Fresno County Board of Supervisors, which voted to sue the state after Gov. Gavin Newsom signed AB 1923 into law last week. In July, Fresno city leaders approved a new General Fund sales tax intended to replace revenue associated with Measure C, which is set to expire in June of next year. The city later withdrew that proposal after state lawmakers approved the legislation. However, after city leaders learned the county's measure had not officially been filed by last Friday's deadline, the city submitted its own transportation tax measure as a backup. Arias said he plans to oppose the city's measure. "I'll be very crystal clear: I intend to vote 'no' on the city's tax measure and to advocate and campaign against the city's tax measure," Arias said. The Better Roads Safe Streets campaign said it expects its measure to appear on the November ballot. With the deadline now passed, the city's transportation tax measure is also set to go before voters. "Families are having to decide between putting food on the table and paying for rent; it's not fair for voters," she said. Councilmember Annalisa Perea also criticized the timing of the special meeting. In a statement, she said: "I am disappointed that four of my colleagues called for a last-minute special meeting considering that this meeting could have been called for late last week. It clearly demonstrates a knee-jerk, sloppy maneuver that could negatively affect the very residents that they represent. This last-minute move impacted preset, existing travel schedules. I consulted with our City Clerk to place me on Zoom so that I could debate this reckless move with my colleagues; however, the timing of this rushed public meeting did not allow us to meet legal noticing requirements that would have afforded me the opportunity to participate by Zoom. They owe the residents an apology." Councilmember Mike Karbassi said he was unable to participate in the meeting because of a serious family medical emergency. Action News also reached out to Councilmembers Nelson Esparza and Tyler Maxwell, but they have not yet responded. City Attorney Andrew Janz said in a statement: "Unfortunately, as of this afternoon, we have confirmed that the County Clerk is still not in possession of all materials necessary to officially place "Better Roads, Safe Streets" on the November ballot," said City Attorney Andrew Janz. "It is also my understanding that the County has filed a lawsuit against County Clerk James Kus to prevent him from placing the "Better Roads, Safe Streets" item on the November ballot. Given the totality of the circumstances and the lingering uncertainty, it makes sense that the Mayor and Council had a backup plan they are now using as a last and final resort." For news updates, follow Ana Torrea on Facebook , X and Instagram .

extraction.body: LAKEWOOD, Ohio (WOIO) - Lakewood City Council held a news conference Friday morning to announce new solutions for what’s been called a dangerous intersection located where Hilliard Road meets Madison Avenue. On Monday, according to Lakewood Fire, a father who was riding his bike with his two young children was struck by a car on Madison Avenue. According to a family member, the three-year-old was hospitalized and may need surgery. In December 2024, retired 19 News Reporter Bill Safos was hit and killed while crossing the street at the same intersection. PREVIOUS COVERAGE: Man charged with vehicular homicide in former Channel 19 reporter’s death Members of Lakewood City Council called a press conference on Friday to discuss their future plans for the intersection. “We’re not going to retreat from our public spaces. We’ve got to hang in there and make this work. We’ve got to hang in there and take it seriously and make it safe,“ said At Large Councilman Tom Bullock. Lakewood Mayor Meghan George said earlier this week part of the plan has already been mapped out and will be put in place when weather permits. Council members announced Friday morning that some of the improvements include painting high visibility sidewalks, repainting bike lanes so they are move obvious, installing traffic calming measures like flowerpots, and continuing to increase the police presence in the area. Matt Bixenstein is one concerned parent who regularly walks his children through the intersection. He says Lakewood is touted as Ohio’s most walkable city, so everyone should feel safe traveling around the municipality. “At the end of the day we need to know as pedestrians and cyclists that we can get to school and work safely just like the motorists can,” says Bixenstein. City council will be bringing an ordinance this week to push the measures through. They also hope to expand Safety Town for educating children about rule of the road and install four-way traffic cameras to better record what is happening in the intersection. While residents are happy the city is taking action, some believe it’s not coming soon enough. “They’ve known about this issue for years. They passed a safe streets ordinance in april of 2024 here we are about 12 months later they’ve done nothing on that issue,” said Brian Higgins of Lakewood. Julie Blantern of Lakewood tells 19 News her mother lives just down the road and is having second thoughts about trying to cross the street to take her young grandchildren to Waga Park. “She’s very concerned and frightened to cross these intersections because of how dangerous they are. I just think a lot of people just aren’t paying attention and could be on their cell phones,” said Blantern. The five-way intersection has a speed limit of 25 mph on Madison Avenue and 35 mph on Hilliard. The city will also be engaging a traffic engineer to study all the problem intersections in Lakewood and come up with long-term solutions to make these areas safer.

Memphis City Council Chief Administrative Officer Takeyshia Johnson on Monday, Oct. 19, circulated a memo to council members and staff titled "ACTION REQUIRED: October 20 Council Meetings| Enhanced Security Procedures" that outlines additional security measures to be taken at the City Council's Tuesday, Oct. 20, and Nov. 10 meetings, as well as committee meetings scheduled to take place in the coming weeks. The memo was filed alongside other court documents related to a temporary restraining order filed by Rep. Justin J. Pearson, who was suspended by the City of Memphis from attending the next two council meetings for his alleged role in the Oct. 9 upheaval. Several other people who attended the Oct. 9 meeting, including at least one council member, have also been suspended from the next two meetings. The security plan outlines additional steps to be taken, including increased security personnel, reserved seating, strict capacity restrictions, and a clear-bag policy. "This work is informed not only by what occurred on October 6, but also by our staff's experiences and concerns," Johnson's email reads. "Since that meeting, staff members have received threats, endured concerning phone calls, and expressed serious concerns about their physical safety and emotional well-being." In addition to the clear-bag policy and reserved seating, under the enhanced security plan, public access to the dais will be restricted, the public speaking podium will be relocated behind the chamber gates, front-row seating will be reserved for "speakers, honorees, presenters and the media," and anyone who is removed for disruptive behavior will not be able to return until at least the following meeting. The plan also halts all unannounced visits to the City Council offices: "Until further notice, access to the Council office will be limited to individuals with confirmed appointments. Walk-ins and unannounced visits will not be permitted." The measures are expected to be in place by Tuesday's council meeting, with some provisions, including restrictions on council chamber access, to remain in effect beyond the two meetings specifically mentioned. extraction.body: The transportation tax measure was intended to fill the gap left by Measure C. Councilmember Miguel Arias called for the special meeting ahead of a 5 p.m. deadline Wednesday. Residents waited about two hours for the meeting to begin before learning no action would be taken. "You called a meeting, we showed up," attendees chanted during the meeting. Another resident said, "They are failing to represent us." Ariana Martinez Lott, a Fresno resident, criticized elected officials for not attending. "What we often see is that when elected officials, when they're campaigning, they're always showing up and they're asking us to support them. Then when they're asked to do their jobs, they play political games this way," Martinez Lott said. Council members Miguel Arias, Brandon Vang and Nick Richardson were present and waiting for another member to arrive. As the deadline approached, it became clear a quorum would not be reached. "We will not be holding a special Fresno City Council meeting today," Vice President Vang announced. Following the meeting, Arias spoke with Action News after the decision. "Our intention was never to have two local taxes for residents in the city of Fresno," Arias said. Wednesday's special meeting follows action taken Tuesday by the Fresno County Board of Supervisors, which voted to sue the state after Gov. Gavin Newsom signed AB 1923 into law last week. In July, Fresno city leaders approved a new General Fund sales tax intended to replace revenue associated with Measure C, which is set to expire in June of next year. The city later withdrew that proposal after state lawmakers approved the legislation. However, after city leaders learned the county's measure had not officially been filed by last Friday's deadline, the city submitted its own transportation tax measure as a backup. Arias said he plans to oppose the city's measure. "I'll be very crystal clear: I intend to vote 'no' on the city's tax measure and to advocate and campaign against the city's tax measure," Arias said. The Better Roads Safe Streets campaign said it expects its measure to appear on the November ballot. With the deadline now passed, the city's transportation tax measure is also set to go before voters. "Families are having to decide between putting food on the table and paying for rent; it's not fair for voters," she said. Councilmember Annalisa Perea also criticized the timing of the special meeting. In a statement, she said: "I am disappointed that four of my colleagues called for a last-minute special meeting considering that this meeting could have been called for late last week. It clearly demonstrates a knee-jerk, sloppy maneuver that could negatively affect the very residents that they represent. This last-minute move impacted preset, existing travel schedules. I consulted with our City Clerk to place me on Zoom so that I could debate this reckless move with my colleagues; however, the timing of this rushed public meeting did not allow us to meet legal noticing requirements that would have afforded me the opportunity to participate by Zoom. They owe the residents an apology." Councilmember Mike Karbassi said he was unable to participate in the meeting because of a serious family medical emergency. Action News also reached out to Councilmembers Nelson Esparza and Tyler Maxwell, but they have not yet responded. City Attorney Andrew Janz said in a statement: "Unfortunately, as of this afternoon, we have confirmed that the County Clerk is still not in possession of all materials necessary to officially place "Better Roads, Safe Streets" on the November ballot," said City Attorney Andrew Janz. "It is also my understanding that the County has filed a lawsuit against County Clerk James Kus to prevent him from placing the "Better Roads, Safe Streets" item on the November ballot. Given the totality of the circumstances and the lingering uncertainty, it makes sense that the Mayor and Council had a backup plan they are now using as a last and final resort." For news updates, follow Ana Torrea on Facebook , X and Instagram .

On Monday, according to Lakewood Fire, a father who was riding his bike with his two young children was struck by a car on Madison Avenue. According to a family member, the three-year-old was hospitalized and may need surgery. In December 2024, retired 19 News Reporter Bill Safos was hit and killed while crossing the street at the same intersection. We’ve got to hang in there and make this work. We’ve got to hang in there and take it seriously and make it safe,“ said At Large Councilman Tom Bullock. Lakewood Mayor Meghan George said earlier this week part of the plan has already been mapped out and will be put in place when weather permits. Council members announced Friday morning that some of the improvements include painting high visibility sidewalks, repainting bike lanes so they are move obvious, installing traffic calming measures like flowerpots, and continuing to increase the police presence in the area. Matt Bixenstein is one concerned parent who regularly walks his children through the intersection. He says Lakewood is touted as Ohio’s most walkable city, so everyone should feel safe traveling around the municipality. “At the end of the day we need to know as pedestrians and cyclists that we can get to school and work safely just like the motorists can,” says Bixenstein. They also hope to expand Safety Town for educating children about rule of the road and install four-way traffic cameras to better record what is happening in the intersection. While residents are happy the city is taking action, some believe it’s not coming soon enough. “They’ve known about this issue for years. They passed a safe streets ordinance in april of 2024 here we are about 12 months later they’ve done nothing on that issue,” said Brian Higgins of Lakewood. Julie Blantern of Lakewood tells 19 News her mother lives just down the road and is having second thoughts about trying to cross the street to take her young grandchildren to Waga Park. “She’s very concerned and frightened to cross these intersections because of how dangerous they are. I just think a lot of people just aren’t paying attention and could be on their cell phones,” said Blantern. The five-way intersection has a speed limit of 25 mph on Madison Avenue and 35 mph on Hilliard. The city will also be engaging a traffic engineer to study all the problem intersections in Lakewood and come up with long-term solutions to make these areas safer.

The group, also known as the Gaitanist Army of Colombia (EGC), launched a wave of violence in recent weeks as part of what it calls its “Plan Pistola” — a terror campaign of targeted killings aimed at both on- and off-duty members of the security forces. Authorities say the murders mark a dangerous escalation by armed groups operating in several departments of the country, including Chocó, Risaralda, Antioquia, Norte de Santander, Cesar and Córdoba. President Petro, accompanied by Defense Minister Pedro Sánchez, will address the nation in a bid to reassure Colombians and outline the government’s response to what he described as a “systematic murder of the people’s children.” “They have killed 27 police officers and soldiers,” Petro posted on social media platform X, alongside photographs of the deceased. “We will not back down. We will intensify the offensive against the Clan. They have no escape route. Either they abandon their illicit activities and reintegrate into a process of regional prosperity under the rule of law and democracy, or a global alliance will be strengthened to destroy the Gulf Clan.” Petro, who has pledged to reach “Total Peace” by negotiating with armed groups, is under intense pressure as violence intensifies across the country. On Friday, Interior Minister Armando Benedetti admitted that the government’s total peace policy “has not gone well,” acknowledging the challenges of negotiating with criminal organizations that continue to operate drug trafficking and extortion networks. Defense Minister Sánchez said the attacks resemble tactics used by drug cartels in the 1980s, including the use of paid assassins, infiltration of local communities, and the carving up of national territory into criminal strongholds. The Gulf Clan maintains influence in northwestern Colombia, while other groups, including the National Liberation Army (ELN) guerrilla, operate along the border departments with Venezuela, among them, Arauca, La Guajira and Norte de Santander. In an interview with the Colombian newspaper El Tiempo , Sánchez confirmed that members of the security forces have been infiltrated by criminal groups, posing a significant challenge to national security. “These groups have managed to penetrate the Armed Forces and the National Police, which means there are criminals inside our institutions,” Sánchez said. “The full weight of the law will be applied. Very likely, in the coming days, several of them will be captured.” Authorities believe that the Gulf Clan has begun subcontracting local gangs to carry out targeted killings, offering financial incentives to execute members of the police and military. The Defense Minister warned that these attacks are part of a broader strategy by the EGC to weaken state institutions and maintain control over strategic drug routes. Monday’s Cabinet meeting will include a review of the government’s current security strategy, with Petro expected to present an assessment of measures implemented since taking office and announce new actions to curb the rising violence. “The goal is to evaluate the security situation and the policies taken, their successes and failures,” Petro said in a brief statement. As officials prepared for the national address, another soldier was killed in a rural area of the municipality of Frontino, Antioquia. According to the military, 23-year-old Alejandro José Bejarano, from Quibdó, Chocó, was fatally shot during a patrol believed to have been ambushed by Gulf Clan members. A second soldier was wounded in the attack and transported to a nearby medical facility. The Gulf Clan, which emerged from the remnants of far-right paramilitary groups, has grown into a powerful drug trafficking network with international links. Although the Petro administration initially opened channels of dialogue with the group, talks were suspended in February after security forces targeted its leadership. One of the group’s top commanders, known as “Chiquito Malo” (Bad Shorty), survived a police operation earlier this year. Days later, another senior figure, known as “Terror,” was killed alongside several bodyguards in a separate raid. Petro’s national address on Monday is expected to outline the next phase of Colombia’s security strategy, as his administration seeks to regain some degree of control over territories increasingly dominated by drug trafficking cartels, trans-nations gangs such as Tren de Aragua (TdeA) and FARC dissidents. A decade later, it was awarded the country's Manuel Murillo Toro medal in communications for contributing to informed and objective coverage of Colombia.

sources.title: Apple teases ‘Pro and Tell’ event for October 28th as touchscreen MacBook Pro anticipation builds - MacDailyNews
passages: Apple marketing chief Greg Joswiak on Monday shared a short teaser video and the message “Can’t wait to pro and tell next week,” confirming the company’s next product experience for Wednesday, October 28th, in Los Angeles.

Gurman has indicated the devices could be introduced around October 28th, with availability potentially following in early November (reports have referenced a possible November 6th window tied to retail preparations).
Earlier speculation about a “MacBook Ultra” name appears to have been walked back, with the touchscreen models expected to remain in the MacBook Pro lineup.
Joswiak’s post, which quickly drew thousands of likes and shares, follows the recent distribution of media invites for an in-person gathering starting at 10 a.m.
• Redesigned 14-inch and 16-inch MacBook Pro models with OLED touchscreens (Apple’s first on a Mac), a Dynamic Island cutout replacing the notch, and a significantly lighter design.
These are widely expected to use M5 Pro and M5 Max chips rather than a new M6 Pro/Max generation.
Joswiak’s playful wording and the fluid logo animation have fueled speculation that the teaser alludes to the tactile or visual qualities of the expected OLED touchscreen machines.
The prospect of a touchscreen MacBook Pro represents a significant departure for Apple, which has long argued against touch input on traditional laptops in favor of trackpad and keyboard precision.
This marks Apple’s second hardware-focused experience of the month.
On October 13th in New York, the company introduced the HomeView smart display, HomePod mini 2, and an updated Apple TV 4K under the “Welcome home” banner.
Until then, the combination of confirmed event timing and consistent high-level reporting has set clear expectations for Apple’s next major hardware step.
— Greg Joswiak (@gregjoz) October 19, 2026

sources.title: Apple CEO Tim Cook teases "big week ahead;" iPhone 17e, new MacBook, and iPads expected to launch
passages: A budget MacBook, refreshed iPads, and the iPhone 17e said to headline next week’s lineupThe star of the show could be Apple's long-rumored lower-cost MacBook — a 12.9-inch laptop powered by the A18 Pro chip (yes, the one from iPhone 16 Pro) with 8GB RAM and fun color options reminiscent of the old iBook days.

The iPhone 17e is expected too, packing an A19 chip, MagSafe, and possibly a Dynamic Island—a solid upgrade over the iPhone 16e at the same $599 price.MacBook Pro may get the Pro and Max chip treatmentRounding things out, Apple is widely expected to launch 14-inch and 16-inch MacBook Pro models with M5 Pro and M5 Max chips.
Apple CEO Tim Cook has confirmed that a wave of product announcements is coming, starting Monday, March 2.

It all starts Monday morning," Cook posted on X, all but confirming what the rumor mill has been churning out for weeks.The company is expected to unveil at least four new products across a three-day stretch, leading up to a hands-on "Apple Experience" event on Wednesday, March 4, in New York, London, and Shanghai.

No design changes are expected — Apple is reportedly saving the big OLED and touchscreen overhaul for the M6 generation later this year.A refreshed Studio Display, new Apple TV, and HomePod mini are also possibilities, though less certain.

The base M5 MacBook Pro dropped back in October, so these higher-end variants have been a matter of when, not if. No design changes are expected — Apple is reportedly saving the big OLED and touchscreen overhaul for the M6 generation later this year.A refreshed Studio Display, new Apple TV, and HomePod mini are also possibilities, though less certain. Either way, it's shaping up to be Apple's busiest product week in a while.

coreStoryFacts.text: But Apple is also planning on revealing a 14-inch MacBook Pro and a new iMac with the M6 chip, which was recently introduced with the Mac Mini.
Apple has sent invites to a second product launch this month, and it’s scheduled for October 28th at 1PM ET in Los Angeles.
Apple’s updated iPad Mini will apparently finally get an OLED screen as well and put the selfie cam on the landscape edge.
Apple’s marketing chief, Greg Joswiak, yesterday announced the date for an upcoming event.
The company’s next product launch event is scheduled for 13 th October, and the event is announced with the tagline “Welcome Home.”
The touch-screen MacBooks are rumoured to feature OLED display panels, lighter than their predecessors and will integrate the Dynamic Island interface previously native to the iPhone line.
Welcome home. October 13. pic.twitter.com/ChelGSDOTI

It is not revealed which products will be revealed at this event, but reports indicate that the company may unveil a dedicated smart display hub, a refreshed HomePod mini, a new Apple TV and Siri AI integrations into the Apple home ecosystem.
After introducing the latest iPhone series last month, Apple is now said to be heading towards the launch of new smart home and core computing products.

Gurman has indicated the devices could be introduced around October 28th, with availability potentially following in early November (reports have referenced a possible November 6th window tied to retail preparations).

These are widely expected to use M5 Pro and M5 Max chips rather than a new M6 Pro/Max generation.
Joswiak’s playful wording and the fluid logo animation have fueled speculation that the teaser alludes to the tactile or visual qualities of the expected OLED touchscreen machines.
The prospect of a touchscreen MacBook Pro represents a significant departure for Apple, which has long argued against touch input on traditional laptops in favor of trackpad and keyboard precision.
This marks Apple’s second hardware-focused experience of the month.
On October 13th in New York, the company introduced the HomeView smart display, HomePod mini 2, and an updated Apple TV 4K under the “Welcome home” banner.
Until then, the combination of confirmed event timing and consistent high-level reporting has set clear expectations for Apple’s next major hardware step.

sources.title: Apple teases ‘Pro and Tell’ event for October 28th as touchscreen MacBook Pro anticipation builds - MacDailyNews
passages: Apple marketing chief Greg Joswiak on Monday shared a short teaser video and the message “Can’t wait to pro and tell next week,” confirming the company’s next product experience for Wednesday, October 28th, in Los Angeles.

Gurman has indicated the devices could be introduced around October 28th, with availability potentially following in early November (reports have referenced a possible November 6th window tied to retail preparations).
Earlier speculation about a “MacBook Ultra” name appears to have been walked back, with the touchscreen models expected to remain in the MacBook Pro lineup.
Joswiak’s post, which quickly drew thousands of likes and shares, follows the recent distribution of media invites for an in-person gathering starting at 10 a.m.
• Redesigned 14-inch and 16-inch MacBook Pro models with OLED touchscreens (Apple’s first on a Mac), a Dynamic Island cutout replacing the notch, and a significantly lighter design.
These are widely expected to use M5 Pro and M5 Max chips rather than a new M6 Pro/Max generation.
Joswiak’s playful wording and the fluid logo animation have fueled speculation that the teaser alludes to the tactile or visual qualities of the expected OLED touchscreen machines.
The prospect of a touchscreen MacBook Pro represents a significant departure for Apple, which has long argued against touch input on traditional laptops in favor of trackpad and keyboard precision.
This marks Apple’s second hardware-focused experience of the month.
On October 13th in New York, the company introduced the HomeView smart display, HomePod mini 2, and an updated Apple TV 4K under the “Welcome home” banner.
Until then, the combination of confirmed event timing and consistent high-level reporting has set clear expectations for Apple’s next major hardware step.
— Greg Joswiak (@gregjoz) October 19, 2026

This marks Apple’s second hardware-focused experience of the month. On October 13th in New York, the company introduced the HomeView smart display, HomePod mini 2, and an updated Apple TV 4K under the “Welcome home” banner. The October 28 gathering in Los Angeles is expected to follow a similar hands-on format for select media and creators rather than a traditional livestreamed keynote, with product announcements and videos likely timed to the event.
Expected Lineup Centers on Mac and iPad Upgrades
While Apple has not confirmed specific products, reporting from Bloomberg News ’ Mark Gurman and coverage across tech outlets points to a Mac- and iPad-focused slate:

• Redesigned 14-inch and 16-inch MacBook Pro models with OLED touchscreens (Apple’s first on a Mac), a Dynamic Island cutout replacing the notch, and a significantly lighter design. These are widely expected to use M5 Pro and M5 Max chips rather than a new M6 Pro/Max generation.
• An entry-level 14-inch MacBook Pro and a refreshed iMac powered by the M6 chip, largely retaining current designs.
• A new iPad mini with an OLED display, a relocated landscape-oriented FaceTime camera, and an updated speaker system.

Earlier speculation about a “MacBook Ultra” name appears to have been walked back, with the touchscreen models expected to remain in the MacBook Pro lineup.

Joswiak’s playful wording and the fluid logo animation have fueled speculation that the teaser alludes to the tactile or visual qualities of the expected OLED touchscreen machines. Apple’s fall product cadence has been busy, following recent iPhone and related launches, and the “Pro and tell” experience appears positioned as a focused showcase for professional and creative users.
Official details will arrive next week. Until then, the combination of confirmed event timing and consistent high-level reporting has set clear expectations for Apple’s next major hardware step.

sources.title: Apple CEO Tim Cook teases "big week ahead;" iPhone 17e, new MacBook, and iPads expected to launch
passages: A budget MacBook, refreshed iPads, and the iPhone 17e said to headline next week’s lineupThe star of the show could be Apple's long-rumored lower-cost MacBook — a 12.9-inch laptop powered by the A18 Pro chip (yes, the one from iPhone 16 Pro) with 8GB RAM and fun color options reminiscent of the old iBook days.

The iPhone 17e is expected too, packing an A19 chip, MagSafe, and possibly a Dynamic Island—a solid upgrade over the iPhone 16e at the same $599 price.MacBook Pro may get the Pro and Max chip treatmentRounding things out, Apple is widely expected to launch 14-inch and 16-inch MacBook Pro models with M5 Pro and M5 Max chips.
Apple CEO Tim Cook has confirmed that a wave of product announcements is coming, starting Monday, March 2.

It all starts Monday morning," Cook posted on X, all but confirming what the rumor mill has been churning out for weeks.The company is expected to unveil at least four new products across a three-day stretch, leading up to a hands-on "Apple Experience" event on Wednesday, March 4, in New York, London, and Shanghai.

No design changes are expected — Apple is reportedly saving the big OLED and touchscreen overhaul for the M6 generation later this year.A refreshed Studio Display, new Apple TV, and HomePod mini are also possibilities, though less certain.

sources.title: Nvidia launches new open models to run agents in the enterprise and on PCs
passages: “Any organization that wants to run agents on Nvidia infrastructure now has an open, optimized model for their tier without having to choose between capability and deployability,” Nvidia’s vice president of Open Models and Software, Kari Briski, wrote in the blog post announcing these models.
The Nemotron 3.5 Super VL is a large, 120-billion-parameter model geared for agents used by the enterprise.
Nvidia on Thursday launched new open-weight models designed for always-on agents and edge computing.

So, while Nvidia hopes to create a new market for itself selling PCs powered by its chips by creating machines that run the models and agents locally, PC users “can delegate everyday projects … without sending those workloads to the cloud,” Briski wrote.
The GPU giant has an entire family of Nemotron models that do everything from multimodal artificial intelligence to reasoning, coding, math, and enterprise automation.
Nvidia claims that the Super VL completes tasks faster than competing models from Anthropic and OpenAI (Opus 5, GPT 6.1 Sol, Luna, Astra) when post-trained on specific agentic tasks.
These tasks include document intelligence, financial accounting, scientific experimentation, medical insurance claims, and security attack resilience.
While such claims are standard whenever a major tech company announces a new model, Nvidia has backed it up with a list of heavy-hitter companies that it says are using Super VL.

Nvidia said the Super VL model is designed for agents in the business domain and can complete tasks faster than competing Anthropic and OpenAI models in post-training-specific tasks such as document intelligence, financial accounting, scientific experimentation, medical insurance claims, and resilience to security attacks. Nvidia also released Bolt models for local deployment on AI PCs using the Nvidia RTX Spark chip and on workstations with the DGX Spark, with Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B 24GB aimed at local tasks and Bolt E4B aimed at conversational agents. The companies’ joint paper identified 30 risk types across five categories and advised enterprises to verify model provenance, test configurations, and reassess risks after material changes, while stating, “Weight openness alone does not determine an AI system’s risk.” A security risk framework lists 30 risk types across five categories Michael Scovetta, Partner Security Assurance Manager at Microsoft, said, “Weight openness alone does not determine an AI system’s risk,” and he added that “Open- and closed-weight models can share many of the same underlying risks, but how those risks materialize depends on the deployment.” The guidance also warned that open-weight models can be fine-tuned, merged, modified, or repackaged, and it cautioned that “Safety behaviors are often the more fragile of the two,” as changes can degrade safeguards while leaving task performance intact. Microsoft and Nvidia recommended using cryptographic signatures to verify that a model matches the publisher’s original artifact, and they advised that “No volume of behavioral testing establishes what an artifact is, only how it behaves.” The guidance said that where signatures are unavailable, organizations should record the unverified integrity as an open risk rather than treating evaluation results as closing it, and it urged monitoring model inputs, outputs, and tool use after deployment. extraction.body: NVIDIA today released Nemotron 3.5 Super VL, an open 120-billion-parameter model that delivers the fastest task completion and highest accuracy for specialized always-on agents. Joining it are two new edge models: Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B 24GB, optimized to balance intelligence and speed per GB for local agentic workloads, and Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B 4GB, optimized for intelligence per GB for fast conversational agents. Super VL and Bolt 74B-A9B are available now, with Bolt E4B coming Oct. 23. The three open models together cover the full range of agent deployments, from large enterprise servers down to edge devices and local hardware. Any organization that wants to run agents on NVIDIA infrastructure now has an open, optimized model for their tier, without having to choose between capability and deployability. Super VL and Bolt join the Nemotron family alongside Lightning and Ultra. Lightning, released in August, handles high-throughput workloads; Ultra handles the hardest reasoning tasks; and Bolt brings intelligence to the edge. Super VL, built in collaboration with the Nemotron Coalition , delivers leading accuracy on multimodal agentic tasks — instruction following, tool use, multistep business workflows, and visual understanding — comparable with NVIDIA’s largest reasoning model at roughly one-fifth the parameter count. As the fastest open agentic model in its class — 5x faster than the next best — it helps enterprise agents complete high-volume tasks faster across workflows that span days or weeks. Unlike closed frontier models, organizations can post-train Super VL on their own data, deploy it on their own infrastructure and oversee what they build. Bolt 74B-A9B 24GB is designed to run everyday agentic tasks locally on NVIDIA RTX/DGX Spark, using a native 2-bit quantization to fit in 24GB of memory and run alongside other applications. With Bolt 74B-A9B 24GB, users can delegate their projects to popular local agent harnesses — from researching the web to writing to debugging code — all without sending those workloads to the cloud. It is the #1 open model in its class on PinchBench , and the #2 open model for BrowseComp . Bolt E4B 4GB is built for physical and conversational agents on GeForce RTX, Jetson, and RTX/DGX Spark. It combines natural conversation with multi-turn agentic capabilities to power fast local voice assistants, interactive characters and embedded interfaces. Dozens of organizations across industries are post-training Super VL on their own data, tools, policies and workflows to push accuracy higher on the specialized tasks that define their agent deployments. Super VL is being post-trained and customized by organizations across industries. Scale AI post-trained the model for Skydance’s vendor credit finance agent and for EY’s M&A due diligence agent. AfterQuery customized the model for Hebbia for credit agreement analysis. AI21 and Alice post-trained the model for cybersecurity attack resilience. Mercor post-trained the model on APEX-SWE coding benchmark, for coding agents that plan, write and debug code. ModelScope enables developers to fine-tune the model through its ms-swift framework for specialized multimodal applications. Additional organizations customizing Nemotron 3.5 Super VL include Ramp for financial document intelligence; Dream , sovereign AI-powered cybersecurity research and vulnerability analysis; Lila Sciences for scientific discovery and search, and R1 for medical claims analysis and revenue cycle management. TrainLoop post-trained the model with dermatology data from Nolla, which just became the first company approved for AI to write initial patient prescriptions. Software platform companies integrating Nemotron 3.5 Super VL include: Nemotron 3.5 Super VL’s vision language strengths are targeted at what agents encounter in practice: optical character recognition, tables, charts and structured information in visual documents. It processes a web page, extracts text, reads graphs and charts, and returns insights from what it finds. The same applies to PDFs and other documents agents commonly work with. Nemotron 3.5 Super VL understands images, webpages and PDFs and acts on that understanding. Combining text and visual understanding in one model means agents don’t need to route tasks between separate systems — context carries through as work moves from document to data to decision. Openness and customizability reinforce each other. The model ships with open weights, open datasets and training recipes. Control runs in two directions. Organizations can run the model wherever their security and data-residency requirements dictate. They also choose to adopt a model they can adapt, rather than one subject to a provider’s restrictions. Customization is supported through NVIDIA NeMo, Python-based pipelines and open datasets. Nemotron 3.5 Super VL was trained on about 26 trillion tokens across pretraining and continued pretraining, then post-trained with roughly 3.8 million samples and reinforcement learning across dozens of environments. NVIDIA is also releasing open datasets on Hugging Face spanning agentic tool use , finance, instruction following, long context, fairness and vision-language understanding, along with the reinforcement learning environments in NeMo Gym. NVIDIA NIM packages the model as a production-ready microservice with performance-optimized, validated configurations and enterprise-grade support, refreshed every two weeks with security patches and performance improvements. And with the model running on NVIDIA Dynamo, organizations can serve up to 8x more users with 85% lower latency. Nemotron 3.5 Super VL is available now on Hugging Face, Open Router, ModelScope community and as NVIDIA NIM. Nemotron 3.5 Super VL runs across NVIDIA’s full hardware stack: on DGX Spark , DGX Station , RTX PRO and RTX systems for local intelligence at the desktop, on NVIDIA Jetson at the edge, and across data center and cloud environments. Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B 24G B is available now on Hugging Face, with support for llama.cpp , Ollama , LM Studio , Unsloth , and vLLM . Built for NVIDIA RTX Spark laptops arriving Oct. 16, it also runs on GeForce RTX PCs , DGX Spark , DGX Station and RTX PRO workstations . Download the open weights , explore customization resources with NVIDIA NeMo, or read the technical blog for the full architecture breakdown. Super VL and Bolt join the Nemotron family alongside Lightning and Ultra.
Lightning, released in August, handles high-throughput workloads; Ultra handles the hardest reasoning tasks; and Bolt brings intelligence to the edge.

Super VL, built in collaboration with the Nemotron Coalition , delivers leading accuracy on multimodal agentic tasks — instruction following, tool use, multistep business workflows, and visual understanding — comparable with NVIDIA’s largest reasoning model at roughly one-fifth the parameter count.
As the fastest open agentic model in its class — 5x faster than the next best — it helps enterprise agents complete high-volume tasks faster across workflows that span days or weeks.
Unlike closed frontier models, organizations can post-train Super VL on their own data, deploy it on their own infrastructure and oversee what they build.
Bolt 74B-A9B 24GB is designed to run everyday agentic tasks locally on NVIDIA RTX/DGX Spark, using a native 2-bit quantization to fit in 24GB of memory and run alongside other applications.

With Bolt 74B-A9B 24GB, users can delegate their projects to popular local agent harnesses — from researching the web to writing to debugging code — all without sending those workloads to the cloud. It is the #1 open model in its class on PinchBench , and the #2 open model for BrowseComp . Bolt E4B 4GB is built for physical and conversational agents on GeForce RTX, Jetson, and RTX/DGX Spark. It combines natural conversation with multi-turn agentic capabilities to power fast local voice assistants, interactive characters and embedded interfaces.

Dozens of organizations across industries are post-training Super VL on their own data, tools, policies and workflows to push accuracy higher on the specialized tasks that define their agent deployments.

Super VL is being post-trained and customized by organizations across industries. Scale AI post-trained the model for Skydance’s vendor credit finance agent and for EY’s M&A due diligence agent. AfterQuery customized the model for Hebbia for credit agreement analysis. AI21 and Alice post-trained the model for cybersecurity attack resilience. Mercor post-trained the model on APEX-SWE coding benchmark, for coding agents that plan, write and debug code. ModelScope enables developers to fine-tune the model through its ms-swift framework for specialized multimodal applications.

Additional organizations customizing Nemotron 3.5 Super VL include Ramp for financial document intelligence; Dream , sovereign AI-powered cybersecurity research and vulnerability analysis; Lila Sciences for scientific discovery and search, and R1 for medical claims analysis and revenue cycle management. TrainLoop post-trained the model with dermatology data from Nolla, which just became the first company approved for AI to write initial patient prescriptions. Software platform companies integrating Nemotron 3.5 Super VL include:
Nemotron 3.5 Super VL’s vision language strengths are targeted at what agents encounter in practice: optical character recognition, tables, charts and structured information in visual documents.
It processes a web page, extracts text, reads graphs and charts, and returns insights from what it finds. The same applies to PDFs and other documents agents commonly work with.

Nemotron 3.5 Super VL understands images, webpages and PDFs and acts on that understanding. Combining text and visual understanding in one model means agents don’t need to route tasks between separate systems — context carries through as work moves from document to data to decision.
Openness and customizability reinforce each other. The model ships with open weights, open datasets and training recipes.

Control runs in two directions. Organizations can run the model wherever their security and data-residency requirements dictate. They also choose to adopt a model they can adapt, rather than one subject to a provider’s restrictions.
Customization is supported through NVIDIA NeMo, Python-based pipelines and open datasets.

Nemotron 3.5 Super VL was trained on about 26 trillion tokens across pretraining and continued pretraining, then post-trained with roughly 3.8 million samples and reinforcement learning across dozens of environments.

NVIDIA is also releasing open datasets on Hugging Face spanning agentic tool use , finance, instruction following, long context, fairness and vision-language understanding, along with the reinforcement learning environments in NeMo Gym.

NVIDIA NIM packages the model as a production-ready microservice with performance-optimized, validated configurations and enterprise-grade support, refreshed every two weeks with security patches and performance improvements.
And with the model running on NVIDIA Dynamo, organizations can serve up to 8x more users with 85% lower latency.
Nemotron 3.5 Super VL is available now on Hugging Face, Open Router, ModelScope community and as NVIDIA NIM.

Nemotron 3.5 Super VL runs across NVIDIA’s full hardware stack: on DGX Spark , DGX Station , RTX PRO and RTX systems for local intelligence at the desktop, on NVIDIA Jetson at the edge, and across data center and cloud environments.

Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B 24G B is available now on Hugging Face, with support for llama.cpp , Ollama , LM Studio , Unsloth , and vLLM . Built for NVIDIA RTX Spark laptops arriving Oct. 16, it also runs on GeForce RTX PCs , DGX Spark , DGX Station and RTX PRO workstations .

sources.title: Nvidia Launches Open AI Models for PCs and Enterprises - Innovation Village
passages: Nvidia has introduced new open-weight artificial intelligence models designed to power enterprise AI agents and run locally on personal computers, expanding its push into AI software and on-device computing.

The new releases include Nemotron 3.5 Super VL, a 120-billion-parameter model built for enterprise agent workflows, and two smaller Nemotron 3.5 Bolt models designed for local deployment on AI PCs and workstations.
The launch builds on Nvidia’s broader Nemotron family, which includes models for reasoning, coding, mathematics, multimodal AI and enterprise automation.

Nvidia’s vice president of Open Models and Software, Kari Briski, said the releases give organisations an open, optimised model for different levels of AI deployment without forcing them to choose between capability and practical implementation.

Nvidia’s open-weight approach gives organisations more flexibility to customise and deploy models, although open weights do not necessarily mean that every part of a model’s training data, development process or software stack is openly available.
Enterprise agents may handle financial records, internal documents, customer information and other confidential data.

The new releases include Nemotron 3.5 Super VL, a 120-billion-parameter model built for enterprise agent workflows, and two smaller Nemotron 3.5 Bolt models designed for local deployment on AI PCs and workstations. The launch reflects Nvidia’s effort to serve businesses that want to run AI systems on their own infrastructure while encouraging the development of personal AI assistants that can operate without sending sensitive information to cloud services. The largest release, Nemotron 3.5 Super VL, is designed for enterprise agents that perform complex tasks involving instructions, documents and external tools. Nvidia says the 120-billion-parameter model can deliver accuracy comparable to its larger Nemotron 3 Ultra model in instruction-following and tool-use tasks, despite having fewer parameters. The company also claims that Super VL can complete specialised agent tasks faster than competing models from Anthropic and OpenAI when post-trained for specific workloads. These applications include document analysis, financial accounting, scientific experimentation, medical insurance claims and cybersecurity testing. Nvidia’s vice president of Open Models and Software, Kari Briski, said the releases give organisations an open, optimised model for different levels of AI deployment without forcing them to choose between capability and practical implementation. The company also identified several organisations using Super VL, including Skydance, EY, Ramp, CrowdStrike, Perplexity and Salesforce. Alongside Super VL, Nvidia introduced two smaller Nemotron 3.5 Bolt models intended to run locally on AI PCs and workstations. The Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B 24GB is a 74-billion-parameter model designed to balance reasoning capabilities with speed. It targets local agent tasks such as multistep reasoning, tool calling and web browsing. The smaller Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B is designed primarily for conversational AI agents. The models are intended for systems built around Nvidia’s RTX Spark chip and DGX Spark workstation platform, giving developers and enterprise users options for running AI workloads directly on their devices. Nvidia said Super VL and Bolt 74B-A9B are available now, while Bolt E4B is expected later in October. The local deployment strategy could appeal to users and businesses concerned about sending sensitive information to external AI services. Enterprise agents may handle financial records, internal documents, customer information and other confidential data. Running models within an organisation’s own infrastructure can give it greater control over how that information is processed. Briski said organisations can post-train Super VL on their own data, deploy it on their own infrastructure and retain control over the systems they build. Local AI assistants could offer similar advantages to consumers who want automated help with everyday tasks without routinely transmitting personal information to cloud-based services. However, running models locally does not automatically guarantee privacy. Security also depends on how applications handle stored information, permissions, network connections and access to files. The launch builds on Nvidia’s broader Nemotron family, which includes models for reasoning, coding, mathematics, multimodal AI and enterprise automation. The company is expanding its model offerings as AI developers increasingly consider alternatives to relying entirely on proprietary models from major AI laboratories. For Nvidia, the strategy also supports demand for its hardware. By developing models optimised for its infrastructure, the company can encourage businesses and consumers to adopt systems built around its chips. At the same time, AI developers are exploring other computing platforms, including Amazon Web Services’ Trainium chips and Cerebras systems, while some companies are developing their own processors. Nvidia’s open-weight approach gives organisations more flexibility to customise and deploy models, although open weights do not necessarily mean that every part of a model’s training data, development process or software stack is openly available. The new releases therefore serve two purposes: helping enterprises run more specialised AI agents on their own infrastructure and bringing local AI capabilities to personal computers. Their adoption will depend on how well the models perform in real-world workloads, the hardware resources they require and the practical benefits they offer over cloud-based alternatives.

coreStoryFacts.text: “Any organization that wants to run agents on Nvidia infrastructure now has an open, optimized model for their tier without having to choose between capability and deployability,” Nvidia’s vice president of Open Models and Software, Kari Briski, wrote in the blog post announcing these models.
The Nemotron 3.5 Super VL is a large, 120-billion-parameter model geared for agents used by the enterprise.
Nvidia on Thursday launched new open-weight models designed for always-on agents and edge computing.

So, while Nvidia hopes to create a new market for itself selling PCs powered by its chips by creating machines that run the models and agents locally, PC users “can delegate everyday projects … without sending those workloads to the cloud,” Briski wrote.
The GPU giant has an entire family of Nemotron models that do everything from multimodal artificial intelligence to reasoning, coding, math, and enterprise automation.
Nvidia claims that the Super VL completes tasks faster than competing models from Anthropic and OpenAI (Opus 5, GPT 6.1 Sol, Luna, Astra) when post-trained on specific agentic tasks.
These tasks include document intelligence, financial accounting, scientific experimentation, medical insurance claims, and security attack resilience.
While such claims are standard whenever a major tech company announces a new model, Nvidia has backed it up with a list of heavy-hitter companies that it says are using Super VL.
These include Skydance, EY, Ramp, Crowdstrike, Perplexity, and Salesforce .
Super VL and Bolt 74B-A9B are available now, with Bolt E4B coming later this month, Nvidia says.

However, those fast-growing proprietary AI labs are now looking to many other chips and AI system makers beyond Nvidia to power their needs, like AWS’s Trainium and Cerebras, as well as building their own home-grown chips.
Nvidia launched new open-weight models for agents in enterprises and on PCs, including the Nemotron 3.5 Super VL with 120 billion parameters and two Bolt models intended to run locally.

Nvidia Vice President of Open Models and Software Kari Briski said in a statement, “any organization that wants to run agents on Nvidia’s infrastructure now has an open model that is optimized for its level without having to choose between capacity and deployability.”

Microsoft and Nvidia urged enterprises to assess the security of open-weight AI models throughout deployment, warning that changes to model weights and configurations can weaken safeguards even when a model retains its ability to perform assigned tasks.

The companies’ joint paper identified 30 risk types across five categories and advised enterprises to verify model provenance, test configurations, and reassess risks after material changes, while stating, “Weight openness alone does not determine an AI system’s risk.”
Nvidia Releases Open-Weight Bolt Model for Local AI Agents
TechCrunch leads with Nvidia’s model launch and deployment, while CSO Online shifts to enterprise risk governance for open-weight adoption.

Gartner recommended routing open-weight model traffic through governed AI gateways to enforce authentication, prompt-injection defenses, sensitive-data protection and audit logging, and it also recommended isolating self-hosted runtimes and applying controls such as private network paths and customer-managed encryption keys for cloud API consumption.

extraction.body: Nvidia on Thursday launched new open-weight models designed for always-on agents and edge computing. The Nemotron 3.5 Super VL is a large, 120-billion-parameter model geared for agents used by the enterprise. While it uses fewer parameters than the Nemotron 3 Ultra model, Nvidia says it can deliver similar accuracy in instruction-following and tool-use tasks. At the other end of the spectrum, the company also launched two lightweight Bolt models. These are intended to run locally on the new AI PCs (running the Nvidia RTX Spark chip) and workstations running the DGX Spark. Such PCs, aimed at consumers, programmers, and enterprise knowledge workers, are being released right now into the market through partners like Microsoft and Dell. “Any organization that wants to run agents on Nvidia infrastructure now has an open, optimized model for their tier without having to choose between capability and deployability,” Nvidia’s vice president of Open Models and Software, Kari Briski, wrote in the blog post announcing these models. Nvidia claims that the Super VL completes tasks faster than competing models from Anthropic and OpenAI (Opus 5, GPT 6.1 Sol, Luna, Astra) when post-trained on specific agentic tasks. These tasks include document intelligence, financial accounting, scientific experimentation, medical insurance claims, and security attack resilience. While such claims are standard whenever a major tech company announces a new model, Nvidia has backed it up with a list of heavy-hitter companies that it says are using Super VL. These include Skydance, EY, Ramp, Crowdstrike, Perplexity, and Salesforce . Of course, these aren’t the first open-weight models that Nvidia has released that compete with the proprietary frontier labs — companies that are both its customers and its investments. The GPU giant has an entire family of Nemotron models that do everything from multimodal artificial intelligence to reasoning, coding, math, and enterprise automation. However, those fast-growing proprietary AI labs are now looking to many other chips and AI system makers beyond Nvidia to power their needs, like AWS’s Trainium and Cerebras, as well as building their own home-grown chips. So Nvidia is leaning hard into the trend of enterprise companies wanting to run their own open models in their own data centers. “Unlike closed frontier models, organizations can post-train Super VL on their own data, deploy it on their own infrastructure and own what they build,” Briski wrote. But with the announcement or the smaller, local PC models, it is also trying to push forward the nascent trend of consumer AI assistants. While it seems a new AI assistant is introduced every day by startups and Big Tech alike, privacy-weary consumers may not want to invite such agents so deeply into their lives giving them access to info about their families, health, finances, and so on. So, while Nvidia hopes to create a new market for itself selling PCs powered by its chips by creating machines that run the models and agents locally, PC users “can delegate everyday projects … without sending those workloads to the cloud,” Briski wrote. Of the two Bolt models, Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B 24GB is a 74-billion parameter model designed for local agentic tasks. It is intended to balance speed with reasoning to handle multistep reasoning, tool calling, and web browsing. The smallest Bolt E4B is aimed at conversational agents. Super VL and Bolt 74B-A9B are available now, with Bolt E4B coming later this month, Nvidia says. extraction.body: NVIDIA today released Nemotron 3.5 Super VL, an open 120-billion-parameter model that delivers the fastest task completion and highest accuracy for specialized always-on agents. Joining it are two new edge models: Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B 24GB, optimized to balance intelligence and speed per GB for local agentic workloads, and Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B 4GB, optimized for intelligence per GB for fast conversational agents. Super VL and Bolt 74B-A9B are available now, with Bolt E4B coming Oct. 23. The three open models together cover the full range of agent deployments, from large enterprise servers down to edge devices and local hardware. Any organization that wants to run agents on NVIDIA infrastructure now has an open, optimized model for their tier, without having to choose between capability and deployability. Super VL and Bolt join the Nemotron family alongside Lightning and Ultra. Lightning, released in August, handles high-throughput workloads; Ultra handles the hardest reasoning tasks; and Bolt brings intelligence to the edge. Super VL, built in collaboration with the Nemotron Coalition , delivers leading accuracy on multimodal agentic tasks — instruction following, tool use, multistep business workflows, and visual understanding — comparable with NVIDIA’s largest reasoning model at roughly one-fifth the parameter count. As the fastest open agentic model in its class — 5x faster than the next best — it helps enterprise agents complete high-volume tasks faster across workflows that span days or weeks. Unlike closed frontier models, organizations can post-train Super VL on their own data, deploy it on their own infrastructure and oversee what they build. Bolt 74B-A9B 24GB is designed to run everyday agentic tasks locally on NVIDIA RTX/DGX Spark, using a native 2-bit quantization to fit in 24GB of memory and run alongside other applications. With Bolt 74B-A9B 24GB, users can delegate their projects to popular local agent harnesses — from researching the web to writing to debugging code — all without sending those workloads to the cloud. It is the #1 open model in its class on PinchBench , and the #2 open model for BrowseComp . Bolt E4B 4GB is built for physical and conversational agents on GeForce RTX, Jetson, and RTX/DGX Spark. It combines natural conversation with multi-turn agentic capabilities to power fast local voice assistants, interactive characters and embedded interfaces. Dozens of organizations across industries are post-training Super VL on their own data, tools, policies and workflows to push accuracy higher on the specialized tasks that define their agent deployments. Super VL is being post-trained and customized by organizations across industries. Scale AI post-trained the model for Skydance’s vendor credit finance agent and for EY’s M&A due diligence agent. AfterQuery customized the model for Hebbia for credit agreement analysis. AI21 and Alice post-trained the model for cybersecurity attack resilience. Mercor post-trained the model on APEX-SWE coding benchmark, for coding agents that plan, write and debug code. ModelScope enables developers to fine-tune the model through its ms-swift framework for specialized multimodal applications. Additional organizations customizing Nemotron 3.5 Super VL include Ramp for financial document intelligence; Dream , sovereign AI-powered cybersecurity research and vulnerability analysis; Lila Sciences for scientific discovery and search, and R1 for medical claims analysis and revenue cycle management. TrainLoop post-trained the model with dermatology data from Nolla, which just became the first company approved for AI to write initial patient prescriptions. Software platform companies integrating Nemotron 3.5 Super VL include: Nemotron 3.5 Super VL’s vision language strengths are targeted at what agents encounter in practice: optical character recognition, tables, charts and structured information in visual documents. It processes a web page, extracts text, reads graphs and charts, and returns insights from what it finds. The same applies to PDFs and other documents agents commonly work with. Nemotron 3.5 Super VL understands images, webpages and PDFs and acts on that understanding. Combining text and visual understanding in one model means agents don’t need to route tasks between separate systems — context carries through as work moves from document to data to decision. Openness and customizability reinforce each other. The model ships with open weights, open datasets and training recipes. Control runs in two directions. Organizations can run the model wherever their security and data-residency requirements dictate. They also choose to adopt a model they can adapt, rather than one subject to a provider’s restrictions. Customization is supported through NVIDIA NeMo, Python-based pipelines and open datasets. Nemotron 3.5 Super VL was trained on about 26 trillion tokens across pretraining and continued pretraining, then post-trained with roughly 3.8 million samples and reinforcement learning across dozens of environments. NVIDIA is also releasing open datasets on Hugging Face spanning agentic tool use , finance, instruction following, long context, fairness and vision-language understanding, along with the reinforcement learning environments in NeMo Gym. NVIDIA NIM packages the model as a production-ready microservice with performance-optimized, validated configurations and enterprise-grade support, refreshed every two weeks with security patches and performance improvements. And with the model running on NVIDIA Dynamo, organizations can serve up to 8x more users with 85% lower latency. Nemotron 3.5 Super VL is available now on Hugging Face, Open Router, ModelScope community and as NVIDIA NIM. Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B 24G B is available now on Hugging Face, with support for llama.cpp , Ollama , LM Studio , Unsloth , and vLLM . Built for NVIDIA RTX Spark laptops arriving Oct. 16, it also runs on GeForce RTX PCs , DGX Spark , DGX Station and RTX PRO workstations . sources.title: Nvidia Launches Open AI Models for PCs and Enterprises - Innovation Village
passages: Nvidia has introduced new open-weight artificial intelligence models designed to power enterprise AI agents and run locally on personal computers, expanding its push into AI software and on-device computing.

The new releases include Nemotron 3.5 Super VL, a 120-billion-parameter model built for enterprise agent workflows, and two smaller Nemotron 3.5 Bolt models designed for local deployment on AI PCs and workstations.
The launch builds on Nvidia’s broader Nemotron family, which includes models for reasoning, coding, mathematics, multimodal AI and enterprise automation.

Nvidia’s vice president of Open Models and Software, Kari Briski, said the releases give organisations an open, optimised model for different levels of AI deployment without forcing them to choose between capability and practical implementation.

Nvidia’s open-weight approach gives organisations more flexibility to customise and deploy models, although open weights do not necessarily mean that every part of a model’s training data, development process or software stack is openly available.
Enterprise agents may handle financial records, internal documents, customer information and other confidential data.

extraction.body: Nvidia has introduced new open-weight artificial intelligence models designed to power enterprise AI agents and run locally on personal computers, expanding its push into AI software and on-device computing. The new releases include Nemotron 3.5 Super VL, a 120-billion-parameter model built for enterprise agent workflows, and two smaller Nemotron 3.5 Bolt models designed for local deployment on AI PCs and workstations. The launch reflects Nvidia’s effort to serve businesses that want to run AI systems on their own infrastructure while encouraging the development of personal AI assistants that can operate without sending sensitive information to cloud services. The largest release, Nemotron 3.5 Super VL, is designed for enterprise agents that perform complex tasks involving instructions, documents and external tools. Nvidia says the 120-billion-parameter model can deliver accuracy comparable to its larger Nemotron 3 Ultra model in instruction-following and tool-use tasks, despite having fewer parameters. The company also claims that Super VL can complete specialised agent tasks faster than competing models from Anthropic and OpenAI when post-trained for specific workloads. These applications include document analysis, financial accounting, scientific experimentation, medical insurance claims and cybersecurity testing. Nvidia’s vice president of Open Models and Software, Kari Briski, said the releases give organisations an open, optimised model for different levels of AI deployment without forcing them to choose between capability and practical implementation. The company also identified several organisations using Super VL, including Skydance, EY, Ramp, CrowdStrike, Perplexity and Salesforce. Alongside Super VL, Nvidia introduced two smaller Nemotron 3.5 Bolt models intended to run locally on AI PCs and workstations. The Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B 24GB is a 74-billion-parameter model designed to balance reasoning capabilities with speed. It targets local agent tasks such as multistep reasoning, tool calling and web browsing. The smaller Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B is designed primarily for conversational AI agents. The models are intended for systems built around Nvidia’s RTX Spark chip and DGX Spark workstation platform, giving developers and enterprise users options for running AI workloads directly on their devices. Nvidia said Super VL and Bolt 74B-A9B are available now, while Bolt E4B is expected later in October. The local deployment strategy could appeal to users and businesses concerned about sending sensitive information to external AI services. Enterprise agents may handle financial records, internal documents, customer information and other confidential data. Running models within an organisation’s own infrastructure can give it greater control over how that information is processed. Briski said organisations can post-train Super VL on their own data, deploy it on their own infrastructure and retain control over the systems they build. Local AI assistants could offer similar advantages to consumers who want automated help with everyday tasks without routinely transmitting personal information to cloud-based services. However, running models locally does not automatically guarantee privacy. Security also depends on how applications handle stored information, permissions, network connections and access to files. The launch builds on Nvidia’s broader Nemotron family, which includes models for reasoning, coding, mathematics, multimodal AI and enterprise automation. The company is expanding its model offerings as AI developers increasingly consider alternatives to relying entirely on proprietary models from major AI laboratories. For Nvidia, the strategy also supports demand for its hardware. By developing models optimised for its infrastructure, the company can encourage businesses and consumers to adopt systems built around its chips. At the same time, AI developers are exploring other computing platforms, including Amazon Web Services’ Trainium chips and Cerebras systems, while some companies are developing their own processors. Nvidia’s open-weight approach gives organisations more flexibility to customise and deploy models, although open weights do not necessarily mean that every part of a model’s training data, development process or software stack is openly available. The new releases therefore serve two purposes: helping enterprises run more specialised AI agents on their own infrastructure and bringing local AI capabilities to personal computers. Their adoption will depend on how well the models perform in real-world workloads, the hardware resources they require and the practical benefits they offer over cloud-based alternatives.
